metadata.title: Claude, Counsel
metadata.topic: CLAUDE BASICS · LEGAL AND FINANCE PLUGINS
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: can Claude screen your legal and financial work for you? Lands the carry-out that legal and finance both screen the first pass, and neither one is the lawyer or the CFO.
metadata.anchor_pair: B01 -> B24 (must be the SAME pair of folders)
metadata.one_flag: N/A — every claim in this reel is a confirmed, present-tense description of what each plugin does, not an inference
metadata.mirror_pair: Act III (Not a Lawyer) / Act V (Not a CFO) — the same four-hard-limits shape, mirrored for each plugin

beats.narration_text: Someone wondered: can Claude screen your legal and financial work? Not quite — it flags the risk in a contract and models the scenario in your numbers, before you commit. Here's what each plugin actually does.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types the naive framing, hesitates on 'DO', corrects to 'screen', lands the real question

props.text:
Can Claude DO
your legal and
financial work?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md. Writer types the newcomer's wrong-guess word 'DO' (implying Claude does the legal/financial work itself), hesitates, corrects to 'screen' -> lands the real question. The wrong guess is picked up directly by Act III ("Not a Lawyer") and Act V ("Not a CFO"). Narration is 35 words + lead_silence_s 0.8, giving the typing a >=9s window (TIMING LAW; the 2026-08-27 pilot's 8-word narration produced a 2.86s open that never showed its own correction).

beats.narration_text: First, what these two plugins have in common.

production_viz.label: The Shared Pattern
production_viz.mechanic: Act-header card: The Shared Pattern

beats.narration_text: Most independent operators sign contracts without reading them closely, and track their finances without ever analyzing them. Not because they're careless — because they're busy, and both of these feel like specialist work.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR PLANTED — two folders, unopened

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR PLANTED — two folders, unopened
production_viz.mechanic: A figure carries two folders labeled Contracts and Finances, neither opened. THIS EXACT PAIR OF FOLDERS RETURNS, opened and labeled, at B24.

beats.narration_text: So the NDA gets signed unread. The vendor terms get accepted because pushing back feels awkward. The receipts pile up in a folder nobody analyzes. This is the gap both plugins are built for.

production_viz.label: The unread stack
production_viz.mechanic: A stack of papers gets signed in a hurry; receipts pile up beside it, untouched.

beats.narration_text: And they share one shape. Neither plugin makes you a professional. Each one gives you a structured first pass — it screens the risk, or accelerates the analysis — and tells you when to bring in a human.

production_viz.label: Screen and accelerate
production_viz.mechanic: Two chips resolve in turn: Screen the risk · Accelerate the analysis.

beats.narration_text: Structured first-pass coverage. It won't catch everything a specialist would — but it catches what you'd otherwise miss entirely, because the honest alternative wasn't a careful review. The alternative was no review at all.

production_viz.label: Better than no review
production_viz.mechanic: Items rain down; a net catches the ones that matter while a few slip past — beside it, an empty net catches nothing.

beats.narration_text: First, the one that reads your contracts.

production_viz.label: The Legal Plugin
production_viz.mechanic: Act-header card: The Legal Plugin

beats.narration_text: The legal plugin is a screening tool. It reads a document against established risk frameworks and flags what deserves your attention — the one clause on the page that could cost you later.

production_viz.label: A screening tool
production_viz.mechanic: A contract page; one clause gets a crimson highlight ring.

beats.narration_text: In practice, you upload a contract and ask plainly: review this agreement and flag any issues — what should I worry about? No legal vocabulary required. Claude reads the whole thing and answers.

production_viz.label: Just ask plainly
production_viz.mechanic: A stylized prompt bar fills with 'Review this agreement and flag any issues — what should I worry about?' and a send arrow fires.

beats.narration_text: What comes back is a risk summary with color-coded flags. Green for standard terms, yellow for items worth a second look, red for real concerns. Each flag explained — what the clause says, why it's flagged, and what you might do about it.

production_viz.label: Green, yellow, red
production_viz.mechanic: Flags sort into three columns by color — green, yellow, red — tallies settling, illustrative not fixed.

beats.narration_text: The screening covers the routine documents a solo operator actually faces: contract review, NDA triage, vendor-agreement analysis, compliance checks — and for yellow or red items, suggested redline language if you decide to negotiate.

production_viz.label: What it screens
production_viz.mechanic: Five chips resolve in turn: Contract review · NDA triage · Vendor terms · Compliance checks · Redline language.

beats.narration_text: And it changes the economics of review. Thorough reading drops from hours to minutes — which is the whole point. It makes contract review a default step, not the exception you skip when you're signing in a hurry.

production_viz.label: Review as default
production_viz.mechanic: A long 'hours' bar collapses past a threshold into a short 'minutes' bar.

beats.narration_text: Now the line you can't cross.

production_viz.label: Not a Lawyer
production_viz.mechanic: Act-header card: Not a Lawyer

beats.narration_text: Because here's what it does not do. It doesn't give legal advice. It doesn't weigh a clause against the strategy of your business. It doesn't replace qualified counsel for significant matters. And it doesn't guarantee its read is legally sound.

production_viz.label: Four hard limits
production_viz.mechanic: Four caution chips resolve in turn: No legal advice · No strategic weighing · No counsel for big deals · No legal guarantee.

beats.narration_text: It's the difference between a screen that catches the obvious problem sitting on the page…

production_viz.label: The screen catches
production_viz.mechanic: A contract under a magnifier, one clause flagged; slow push toward the flag.

beats.narration_text: …and outside counsel who tells you whether to sign. For routine work — the NDA, the SaaS terms, the freelancer agreement you reuse — screening beats no review at all. For high-stakes deals, call a lawyer. The plugin helps you know which one you're in.

production_viz.label: Counsel makes the call
production_viz.mechanic: Continuous move to a second desk — a professional marking up the contract; same room grammar as B11.

beats.narration_text: That's the real skill it hands you: triage. Routine and low-stakes, the screen is enough. Complex, or high-stakes, and a red flag is your signal to escalate — to a person, before you sign.

production_viz.label: Know which you're in
production_viz.mechanic: One contract enters a fork: routine flows down to the screen; high-stakes routes up to a human.

beats.narration_text: Now the one that reads your numbers.

production_viz.label: The Finance Plugin
production_viz.mechanic: Act-header card: The Finance Plugin

beats.narration_text: The finance plugin brings financial analysis into Claude. Its real value isn't the deep dive — it's turning analysis into something you actually do, instead of something you keep meaning to do.

production_viz.label: Actually do it
production_viz.mechanic: A solo operator at night over a laptop and printed statements; slow push-in.

beats.narration_text: You point Claude at your data and ask the questions you've been putting off. Here's six months of revenue and expenses — what's my burn rate, and how long is my runway at this pace?

production_viz.label: Aim at your data
production_viz.mechanic: The prompt bar fills with 'Here's 6 months of revenue and expenses. What's my burn rate and runway?' and fires.

beats.narration_text: From there it does the kind of analysis a fractional CFO would: budget and variance tracking, revenue forecasting, expense trends, simple modeling, and clean reports — for you, or for a lender or investor.

production_viz.label: What it analyzes
production_viz.mechanic: Five chips resolve in turn: Budget & variance · Forecasting · Expense trends · Modeling · Reports.

beats.narration_text: The health check first: your monthly burn rate, and your runway — how many months the cash lasts at the current pace. The number you keep avoiding, made plain in seconds.

production_viz.label: Burn and runway
production_viz.mechanic: A cash bar drains month by month toward zero; the runway length reads out as it empties.

beats.narration_text: Then the part that earns its keep: scenario modeling. Raise prices by, say, fifteen percent — where's the break-even? Hire a contractor who helps you land more clients — how long until the hire pays for itself? Claude models best, likely, and worst case, shows the math, and you adjust the assumptions and rerun.

production_viz.label: Best, likely, worst
production_viz.mechanic: Three payback curves — best, likely, worst — climb toward a break-even line at different speeds.

beats.narration_text: And the line on this side.

production_viz.label: Not a CFO
production_viz.mechanic: Act-header card: Not a CFO

beats.narration_text: The limits, just as plainly. It won't file your taxes. It won't give you accounting advice. It won't replace a bookkeeper for complex records. And it won't guarantee its numbers are accurate for a regulator.

production_viz.label: Four hard limits
production_viz.mechanic: Four caution chips resolve in turn: Won't file taxes · No accounting advice · No bookkeeping · No regulatory guarantee.

beats.narration_text: It builds the model — but it can't tell you the assumptions fit your industry, or that the figure will hold up to the taxman. The math is fast; the judgment is yours.

production_viz.label: The judgment is yours
production_viz.mechanic: A person pauses over a hiring decision and a spreadsheet; a crimson ring draws on around the person.

beats.narration_text: So the finance plugin gives you the analysis a CFO would produce — but the consequential call stays with a human, and for real stakes, a real accountant signs off. An accelerator, not a CFO.

production_viz.label: The call stays human
production_viz.mechanic: A finished model flows toward a decision point where a human — not the plugin — makes the call.

beats.narration_text: Last — how to actually get the value.

production_viz.label: Make It Routine
production_viz.mechanic: Act-header card: Make It Routine

beats.narration_text: Three habits make both worth it. Run them routinely, not occasionally — the value is in the habit. Treat every red flag as a signal to escalate. And keep your documents organized, so Claude can actually find them.

production_viz.label: Three habits
production_viz.mechanic: Three panels light in turn: Routine, not occasional · Escalate the red flags · Organized documents.

beats.act: ACT VI — 5 direction A (why routine wins)
beats.narration_text: Because the value isn't the one-off deep dive — it's catching problems early. A bad clause, a financial trend that doesn't add up: the cost of fixing it climbs the longer it hides. Monthly reviews and automatic screening catch it while it's still cheap.

production_viz.label: Early is cheapest
production_viz.mechanic: A cost curve rises steeply over time; an early catch sits low on the curve, a late catch far up it.

beats.narration_text: And the simplest lever of all: a folder of contracts, a folder of financial records, consistently kept. The more easily Claude can find them, the more useful both plugins become.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — folders, labeled and open

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — folders, labeled and open
production_viz.mechanic: THE SAME TWO FOLDERS FROM B01 return, now open and neatly labeled — Contracts, Finances — on a tidy desk.

beats.narration_text: Legal and finance both screen the first pass — neither one is the lawyer or the CFO.

production_viz.label: THE CARRY-OUT — one sentence, alone
production_viz.mechanic: The carry-out sentence, alone on screen, serif, large. Nothing else in frame.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. I run a one-person business. I'm about to sign a vendor contract and set next quarter's budget. Act as my first-pass screen, not my lawyer or my CFO: tell me what to paste in so the legal plugin can flag the concerning clauses, show me the three scenarios the finance plugin should model before I commit to a new hire, and for each, name the exact moment I should stop and call a real lawyer or accountant.

beats.narration_text: Claude, Counsel.
